title: Rhythm for Sale: the song he wrote
summary: Tape 3 side B; he says he wrote the opening song about the history of the Negro, and Nierenberg reads the lyrics.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: "Rhythm for Sale" who wrote that song?
Well this is the song you said tells the story of negro life?
Almost, the history of the negro in the world.

Years ago a certain sage
Said the whole world is a stage
And we are the players from
the start
If its so the colored folks
With their songs and dances,
and jokes in this show
Must play a special part

All the world wants rhythm bad
Colored folks are might glad
'Cause they've got rhythm for sale

Everyone will hum a song
Our tune will carry on
We've got rhythm for sale.

Up in Harlem they are doing swell
Nature gave them something they
can sell
Everybody on this earth
Is in joy of song and mirth
We've got rhythm for sale.

You like that
song? And there's another verse to that song.
That's a classic that

Since the emancipation came
Jungle rhythm has made a name
But the terms ain't quite the same
'Cause we've got rhythm for sale.

M-m-m -- left me that quick.
Can't think of the rest of that. I'll have to
write it out and let you put it in.
Where can we go from there
now?
